the change of a solid into a liquid on heating
the state of matter with a definite volume but no definite shape
the state of matter that spreads out to fill any container
items.s: liquid: the state of matter with a definite volume but no definite shape. The other options describe solid, melting, gas.
items.t: States of matter and change of state

items.q: liquid may be defined as
o: the state of matter that spreads out to fill any container
the change of a vapour into a liquid on cooling
the state of matter with a definite volume but no definite shape
the state of matter with a definite shape and a definite volume
items.s: liquid: the state of matter with a definite volume but no definite shape. The other options describe condensation, gas, solid.
items.t: States of matter and change of state

items.q: Which statement correctly defines specimen?
o: a room equipped for practical work and experiments in science
a large sheet of drawn information displayed before a class
any material or device used to support the teaching of science
a sample of a plant or animal or material kept for study
items.s: specimen: a sample of a plant or animal or material kept for study. The other options describe chart, instructional resource, laboratory.

items.q: “the SI base unit used for measuring thermodynamic temperature” is the definition of
o: metre
second
mole
kelvin
items.s: kelvin is the SI base unit used for measuring thermodynamic temperature.

items.q: “the SI base unit used for measuring length or distance” is the definition of
o: metre
derived unit
measurement
SI unit
items.s: metre is the SI base unit used for measuring length or distance.

items.q: “the assignment of a number and a unit to a physical quantity” is the definition of
o: measurement
derived unit
metre
candela
items.s: measurement is the assignment of a number and a unit to a physical quantity.

items.q: In this course, melting refers to
o: the change of a vapour into a liquid on cooling
the direct change of a solid into a gas without melting
the state of matter with a definite volume but no definite shape
the change of a solid into a liquid on heating
items.s: melting: the change of a solid into a liquid on heating. The other options describe liquid, condensation, sublimation.
items.t: States of matter and change of state

items.q: living thing may be defined as
o: an organism that carries out all the processes of life
an object that does not carry out any process of life
a single living body such as a plant or an animal
an activity that a living thing must carry out to stay alive
items.s: living thing: an organism that carries out all the processes of life. The other options describe non-living thing, life process, organism.

items.q: reproduction may be defined as
o: the ability of a living thing to respond to a change around it
the process by which living things produce new individuals of their kind
the taking in of food materials needed for growth and energy
a change in position or place by a living thing
items.s: reproduction: the process by which living things produce new individuals of their kind. The other options describe nutrition, irritability, movement.

items.q: The correct meaning of volume is
o: the amount of space occupied by a body or substance
a feature that describes how a substance reacts with other substances
the amount of matter contained in a body
anything that has mass and occupies space
items.s: volume: the amount of space occupied by a body or substance. The other options describe mass, matter, chemical property.

items.q: “an object or picture that helps a learner understand a science idea” is the definition of
o: teaching aid
specimen
chart
laboratory
items.s: teaching aid is an object or picture that helps a learner understand a science idea.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines candela?
o: the SI base unit used for measuring luminous intensity
the SI base unit used for measuring the amount of a substance
the SI base unit used for measuring thermodynamic temperature
the SI base unit used for measuring time
items.s: candela: the SI base unit used for measuring luminous intensity. The other options describe mole, second, kelvin.

items.q: In this course, predicting refers to
o: an observation that describes a feature without using any number
the process of comparing a quantity with an agreed standard unit
an observation that records a feature by means of a number
the stating of what is expected to happen in a future event
items.s: predicting: the stating of what is expected to happen in a future event. The other options describe qualitative observation, measuring, quantitative observation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the SI base unit used for measuring the amount of a substance”
o: measurement
mole
ampere
metre
items.s: mole is the SI base unit used for measuring the amount of a substance.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the change of a vapour into a liquid on cooling”
o: gas
liquid
condensation
solid
items.s: condensation is the change of a vapour into a liquid on cooling.
items.t: States of matter and change of state

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an observation that describes a feature without using any number”
o: predicting
measuring
estimation
qualitative observation
items.s: qualitative observation is an observation that describes a feature without using any number.

items.q: SI unit may be defined as
o: the standard unit agreed internationally for measuring a physical quantity
a unit obtained by combining two or more base units together
the SI base unit used for measuring time
the assignment of a number and a unit to a physical quantity
items.s: SI unit: the standard unit agreed internationally for measuring a physical quantity. The other options describe second, derived unit, measurement.

items.q: In this course, metre rule refers to
o: a tall glass vessel marked in divisions for measuring liquid volume
an instrument that compares the mass of a body with standard masses
a flat strip marked in divisions and used for measuring length
a device made for taking a measurement or making an observation
items.s: metre rule: a flat strip marked in divisions and used for measuring length. The other options describe beam balance, measuring cylinder, instrument.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains integrated approach.
o: the organised body of knowledge built from observation and experiment
the teaching of related ideas from biology and chemistry and physics as one whole
a testable explanation suggested before an investigation is carried out
the application of scientific knowledge to make tools and solve problems
items.s: integrated approach: the teaching of related ideas from biology and chemistry and physics as one whole. The other options describe hypothesis, technology, science.

items.q: The correct meaning of measurement is
o: a unit obtained by combining two or more base units together
the SI base unit used for measuring thermodynamic temperature
the assignment of a number and a unit to a physical quantity
the SI base unit used for measuring the amount of a substance
items.s: measurement: the assignment of a number and a unit to a physical quantity. The other options describe mole, derived unit, kelvin.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines accuracy?
o: a tall glass vessel marked in divisions for measuring liquid volume
an instrument that compares the mass of a body with standard masses
a flat strip marked in divisions and used for measuring length
the closeness of a measured value to the true value
items.s: accuracy: the closeness of a measured value to the true value. The other options describe beam balance, metre rule, measuring cylinder.
